title: Greeting with a Default
oneLiner: Write a function with an optional parameter, clean up its input, and build the result with string interpolation.
keyTakeaway: A default value makes a parameter optional: string greeting = "Hello" in C#, greeting="Hello" in Python. Clean inputs (trim, check for empty) at the top of a function so the rest of it can trust them.
explanation:
Write Greet(name, greeting) returning "<greeting>, <name>!". The greeting is optional and defaults to "Hello", so Greet("Ada") gives "Hello, Ada!" and Greet("Ada", "Welcome back") gives "Welcome back, Ada!". Trim spaces from the start and end of the name, and if nothing is left, use "stranger" instead.

Give the second parameter a default value in the function's definition: string greeting = "Hello" in C#, greeting="Hello" in Python. Then clean the name first: name.Trim() / name.strip(), and check whether the result is empty (string.IsNullOrEmpty(trimmed) or trimmed.Length == 0 in C#; if not trimmed: in Python, since an empty string is falsy). Finally build the result with interpolation: $"{greeting}, {trimmed}!" or f"{greeting}, {trimmed}!".

The tests call the function both with and without the second argument, so the default really has to be there. Until you add it, running the starter code fails before any test runs: C# reports error CS7036 (no argument given for the required parameter 'greeting') and Python raises a TypeError about a missing argument. That message is the language telling you exactly what this exercise is about.

    # TODO: trim the name; use "stranger" if it's empty.

visualizationSteps.message: Called as Greet("  Linus ") with no greeting, so greeting takes its default, "Hello".
Trim the spaces from both ends.
Not empty, so keep it. ("   " would trim to "" and become "stranger".)
Interpolate: greeting, a comma and space, the name, an exclamation mark.

complexity.note: Trimming and building the result touch each character of the name and greeting once; the result string is the extra space. For short names that is effectively constant.

referenceSolutions.python:
def greet(name, greeting="Hello"):
    trimmed = name.strip()
    if not trimmed:  # an empty string is falsy
        trimmed = "stranger"
    return f"{greeting}, {trimmed}!"
